patientSpecificClaim: The exact dollar figure of the allowed amount for a specific procedure or service.
Whether a specific provider is in-network and thus bound to accept the allowed amount without balance billing.
The difference between the billed charge and the allowed amount for a specific claim.
The specific amounts billed, allowed, paid, and owed for a given encounter.
The specific remark codes and denial reasons applied to a claim.
Whether the patient has already paid a portion of the balance shown on the EOB (e.g., a copay collected at the point of service).
The specific dollar amount of the patient's deductible.
How much of the deductible has been met to date.
Whether the patient's specific plan waives the deductible for certain services (e.g., primary care visits, prescription drugs).
Whether a family plan uses an aggregate or embedded deductible structure.
The specific coinsurance percentage for a given service or tier.
The exact dollar amount owed for coinsurance on a specific claim (which requires knowing the allowed amount).
Whether the deductible has been met, triggering the coinsurance phase.
The specific copay amount for a particular service category (e.g., ER visit vs. primary care).
Whether the copay applies before or after the deductible for that specific service under that specific plan.
The specific dollar limit of the out-of-pocket maximum for the individual or family.
The current accumulated total toward the out-of-pocket maximum.
Whether a family plan has embedded individual maximums (required for ACA plans if the family max exceeds the statutory individual limit).
